attempts.summary: Implemented an Ansible playbook, run from node2 (the configured control_node, which has ansible-core installed) against node1, that serves a package repository from local storage on node1 and installs a package (cowsay) from it while the usual remote Ubuntu apt mirrors are unreachable. The playbook staged the .deb via apt-get download into /srv/local-repo, built a Packages index with apt-ftparchive, registered a trusted file:// apt source, made the remote mirrors unreachable by redirecting their hostnames to 127.0.0.1 in /etc/hosts (a reversible disruption), ran apt-get update and captured its output showing connection-refused errors for archive.ubuntu.com/security.ubuntu.com alongside successful reads from the local repo, installed cowsay purely from the local repo, verified it runs, then restored /etc/hosts and re-verified remote reachability. Completed the mandatory one-node-at-a-time restart protocol for both node1 and node2: captured pre-restart boot IDs and service/data health, issued systemctl reboot via a backgrounded ack-then-disconnect pattern, polled until each node was reachable again, and proved changed boot IDs plus recovered SSH/Ansible connectivity, the intact local repo, and the still-installed/functional cowsay package on node1 after its reboot.
